subject: Clarification: prompt & backup deletion timelines (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Michael O'Connor <moconnor@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com

Subject: Data retention specifics for prompts, logs and backups

Hi Lauren,

Hope you are well. Our Data Protection Officer is reviewing Redwood as part of the Acme Health procurement checklist and had a few follow-ups specifically about retention and deletion mechanics that we need to close before procurement sign-off. Could you confirm the following details (ideally with supporting artifacts):

- Retention windows: what are the default retention periods for (a) raw prompts / request/response payloads, (b) application/audit logs, (c) aggregated telemetry, and (d) backups / immutable snapshots?
- Backups: are backups (full snapshots) included in your DPA retention scope? If a deletion request is issued for a customer record, how and when is that data removed from backups/immutable snapshots?
- Prompt cache / KV cache: is prompt data cached anywhere beyond the immediate request (e.g., for routing, replay, or evals)? If so, what TTLs and redaction steps are applied?
- Evidence: we need an S3 lifecycle or bucket policy screenshot + a short narrative describing the deletion workflow, plus any SOC 2 control IDs that map to backup and deletion controls.

As background, Acme's DPA expects prompt-level PII to be removable within 30 days of a deletion request and backups to be purged within a defined window (Acme prefers 90 days but would consider up to 180 days with appropriate controls). Also confirm whether you can accept a DPA amendment to align backup retention.

Can you get back to me by next week with a short summary and artifacts? If it's easier, happy to hop on a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Data Protection Officer
Acme Health
elena.ruiz@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: Data retention specifics for prompts, logs and backups

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Dev (security) and Hannah (legal) to provide the technical and DPA amendment details. High-level responses below; we'll attach the evidence you asked for in our next message.

High-level retention summary (current default configurations):
- Prompts / request/response payloads: ephemeral cache TTL = 7 days (short-term troubleshooting and dedup). Aggregated prompt logs kept for 30 days by default for debugging and quality monitoring; these are encrypted at rest.
- KV/cache (runtime): instance-level KV cache rotates every 24 hours; no persistent cross-tenant persistent prompt replay storage unless customer enables evaluation logging.
- Application/audit logs: 365 days (audit trails / security investigations).
- Backups / snapshots: weekly full snapshots; snapshot retention default = 180 days. We maintain immutable snapshots via Object Lock for a 90-day immutable window by default; cold-region backups are retained up to 365 days for disaster recovery (configurable per-account).

Deletion & backups: a customer-initiated deletion request immediately marks records as deleted in the live store and triggers an async redaction workflow. For backups/snapshots, we rely on our backup retention policy: live deletions are applied to the primary store immediately; backups are removed per their lifecycle rules (so full garbage-collection of all historical copies may take up to the configured backup-retention window — typically <=180 days). We can discuss shortening the backup retention window for Acme in the DPA amendment.

Next steps: Dev will follow up with the specific artifacts (S3 lifecycle policy, backup-rotation diagram, and a short SOC 2 control mapping). Hannah will advise on DPA amendment language and whether Acme's 90-day preference is feasible under our current operations.

Attachments forthcoming: redwood_retention_policy_v2.pdf, s3-lifecycle-policy.txt, backup-rotation-diagram.png, draft DPA amendment.

Would you prefer we propose a drafted amendment with 180 days and include additional compensating controls (encryption + Object Lock + monthly scrub reports), or try for 90 days with a different set of compensating controls?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data retention specifics for prompts, logs and backups

Elena / Lauren — adding the technical detail and evidence pointers. TL;DR: we can support a 90–180 day backup retention window depending on the controls you require; prompt-level PII is not kept longer than the prompt logs TTL unless you opt in to eval logging.

Technical details:
- Prompt storage: incoming request payloads are written to an encrypted request bucket for immediate processing. Ephemeral cache TTL = 7 days. Aggregated prompt logs are retained 30 days by default; these are stored in a tenant-scoped, KMS-encrypted bucket.
- KV cache & runtime: KV cache is memory-backed with fallback to ephemeral local disk; instances scrub local cache on rotation; nothing in KV cache is replicated to long-term storage by default.
- Backups/snapshots: weekly full snapshots written to 'redwood-backups' multi-region bucket. Backups are encrypted with CMKs and have lifecycle rules: transition to cold storage after 30 days, delete after 180 days (account default). For additional immutability we apply Object Lock for 90 days to protect from accidental deletion; immutable copies in cold-region may be retained longer (up to 365 days) if an account requires it.
- Deletion workflow: 1) Live-store delete marks record deleted and strips PII; 2) Nightly redaction job rewrites affected objects to remove PII where feasible; 3) Backup purge is governed by lifecycle — any full historical copy may remain until its retention expiry; we provide a 'backup purge acknowledgement' report when the records are fully removed from backup-set (this can take up to the backup retention window).

Evidence we can produce for you:
- Screenshot: bucket lifecycle policy (attached: s3-lifecycle-policy.txt)
- Architecture diagram: backup rotation & immutable snapshot flow (attached: backup-rotation-diagram.png)
- Export: sample retention audit showing object deletion events and GC runs (we can redact tenant IDs)
- SOC 2 mapping: CC6 (system operations), CC7 (change control) mapping doc (will include in attachments)

Controls and compensations for a shorter backup window (90d):
- Object Lock + WORM in production buckets for a 90d immutable period
- Monthly integrity scans & monthly backup purge confirmation report to Acme
- Encrypted backups with CMK, strict access controls and quarterly access review

If Acme's DPO is comfortable with a 180-day backup retention provided we commit to monthly purge reporting and an explicit DPA clause on backup handling, we can draft that amendment. Otherwise, for 90 days we will require Object Lock + additional reporting commitments.

Attachments: redwood_retention_policy_v2.pdf (policy summary), s3-lifecycle-policy.txt (policy export), backup-rotation-diagram.png

—Dev
